payload.text:
I reviewed the `excerpt-helper` branch against `main` (2 commits) and didn't change anything. The tests pass, but they only check the happy path. **I wouldn't merge yet: there's one real bug that will show on most cards.**

**Blocker**
1. **Short text always gets an ellipsis.** `excerpt()` never checks whether the text already fits, so it adds "…" every time. When I ran it, `excerpt('short', 50)` returned `"short…"` and an empty body returned `"…"`. The README promises the ellipsis "appears only when text was actually removed", so the code breaks its own spec. The fix is to return `trimmed` unchanged when `trimmed.length <= limit`.

**Should fix**
2. **An exact word boundary is missed by one.** `lastSpaceBefore` only searches `text.slice(0, limit)`, so it never sees a space sitting right at position `limit`. When I ran `excerpt('the quick brown', 9)`, it returned `"the…"` instead of `"the quick…"`. The README says the cut is "at or before the limit", so it should search `slice(0, limit + 1)`.
3. **`toPlain` removes characters from inside words.** `[*_~`]` strips every underscore and asterisk, not just formatting markers. `my_var_name` came out as `myvarname`, which matters for a snippet app. It also mishandles images: `![img](u.png)` came out as `!img`.

**Minor**
4. The CHANGELOG quietly rewords the old 1.4.0 entry ("a title and a body" → "title and body"). Past release notes probably shouldn't be edited.
5. The tests don't cover text under the limit, empty input, a space exactly at the limit, or markdown inside words. Those would have caught items 1–3.

The 1.5.0 version bump and the README text look fine.
